value.first: To move a 2-year-old out of your bed and into her own room, I'd use the chair method (also called camping out). It was tested in the same trial program whose five-year follow-up found no harm, and it suits a toddler in a new room better than closed-door waits. If she's in a crib and you can handle timed crying, graduated check-ins (the Ferber method) is the faster version, about a week.
value.second: Nights 1-3: pick a bedtime between 6:30 and 8 and keep it. Do the same 20-30 minute routine in her room: bath, book, bed. Put her down awake and sit in a chair right beside her. Calm voice, minimal touch, no rocking or lying down with her. Nights 4-6: chair mid-room. Then by the door, then the hallway in view, about every 3 nights. Expect protest, and maybe a worse night 2 or 3. That's the old habit breaking.
value.third: If she wakes at night, walk her back to her own room and sit in that night's chair spot. Never lock or hold her door shut. It's working when she settles faster even as the chair moves away; most families need 2-3 weeks. If you notice snoring, gasping or pauses in her breathing during sleep, that's worth a doctor's look.
